rules.statement: The mere duration of possession alone is insufficient to establish a presumption of ouster in favor of a co-owner, unless there are additional circumstances that tend to show the probability of an ouster and the difficulty or impossibility of adducing proof of it.
rules.supporting_quote: "If the ratio decidendi of the decision in Rajapakse v. Hendrick Singho is that acquiescence, on the part of a purchaser of an undivided interest, in the exclusive possession of the entire land and the appropriation of its profits by the other co-owner, is a circumstance from which the adversity of the possession of the other co-owners can be inferred, then that decision may be in consonance with the dicta of Bertram C.J. and Ennis J. to which I have earlier referred."
